name: LearnWorlds
tagline: Online courses, interactive video, communities, websites, and mobile apps

pricing.basis: monthly course plan plus transaction fee
pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited users and paid courses; 1 admin; 3-page website; $5 fee per paid course enrollment.

tiers.name: Pro Trainer
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; 5 admins; unlimited site pages; 0 LearnWorlds transaction fee.

tiers.name: Learning Center
tiers.limits: Unlimited users; 25 admins; 0 LearnWorlds transaction fee.

tiers.name: High Volume & Corporate
tiers.limits: Custom users, admins, SLAs and scale; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.hiddenCosts: Starter charges $5 for every paid course enrollment; the white-label mobile app is $149/month on eligible tiers; school content syncing is $149/month on Pro Trainer and cross-school syncing is $149/month on Learning Center; processors charge separately.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. LearnWorlds's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow course platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
production codecs, rendering speed, and media templates
whyPeopleStillPay: LearnWorlds: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Courses, quizzes, drip lessons, communities and a site in one compose stack; interactive-video polish is thinner.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit cannot match LearnWorlds' interactive-video tooling, native mobile experience or polished engagement analytics.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Frappe Learning
alternatives.desc: A modern course platform with video, quizzes, assignments, cohorts, discussions and payments; mobile apps are not included.

facts.install: Run Frappe's easy-install script or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.dataFormat: Course and user records in the Frappe/MariaDB site database; public/private site files on disk, while video lessons commonly embed external hosts
facts.gapVsPaid: Frappe Learning lacks LearnWorlds' interactive-video authoring, branded mobile apps and polished learner-engagement tooling.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting still needs Docker or a Frappe server, DNS/SSL and email; payments require separate gateway configuration

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: A real LMS with lessons, progress, quizzes, forums, H5P and mobile apps; the interface has opinions from several geological eras.

facts.install: Upload the PHP release to a web server, create a database and moodledata directory, then complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Courses, users, grades and settings in SQL; uploaded files in the separate moodledata directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Moodle's interface and content workflow are less polished, and interactive video/mobile branding require extensions and administration.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and database requirements, protected writable storage, cron, SMTP, backups and upgrades are all the operator's responsibility

alternatives.name: Odoo Community
alternatives.desc: Website, paid courses, forums and business plumbing in one enormous box; native mobile-course polish is not its party trick.

facts.install: Use Odoo's packaged installer, source install or Docker image, backed by PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Business and website records in PostgreSQL; uploaded attachments in Odoo's filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo does not match LearnWorlds' interactive video, mobile learning, community or specialized engagement tooling.
facts.setupBlocker: A production deployment needs PostgreSQL, workers/reverse proxy configuration, backups and ongoing administration of a very large suite

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ghost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A fine membership publisher, not an LMS with progress, quizzes, assignments or interactive lessons.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Commerce infrastructure does not become a course platform merely because courses can be sold.

notes: Credibility row: LearnWorlds survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by LearnWorlds; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow course platform storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations; native apps and community moderation; fulfilment, email, and affiliate ecosystems.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
